name: ScaleOut StateServer
tagline: Commercial in-memory data grid for .NET and Java with parallel query, Redis support and in-cache code.
description: ScaleOut StateServer is the in-memory data grid at the core of ScaleOut Software's product suite, sold since the mid-2000s and long popular as a distributed ASP.NET session and object cache. It partitions objects across a cluster of Windows or Linux servers, keeps up to three replicas of each, and rebalances and self-heals automatically as servers join or fail. Objects can be indexed and queried in parallel (LINQ from C#, filter methods from Java and C++), and the grid also implements the core Redis data structures and pub/sub using open-source Redis code. Version 6 of the suite (September 2025) added Active Caching, which hosts application modules inside the cache, alongside existing digital-twin and streaming products. It is commercial, quote-priced software aimed mainly at .NET enterprises.

pricing.notes: Quote-based licensing; a free trial is available for Windows and Linux.

scale.notes: Partitions data across a cluster with up to three replicas per object; adding a server triggers automatic rebalancing. Separate products add WAN replication.

strengths: Mature, self-healing in-memory grid with automatic partitioning and up to three replicas
Parallel, indexed queries over cached objects using LINQ or Java filters
Implements core Redis data structures and pub/sub on the same grid
Active Caching runs application code inside the cache to cut network round trips
First-class ASP.NET and Java session-state providers
weaknesses: Much smaller community than Redis, Hazelcast or Apache Ignite
Persistence relies on backing-store integration rather than a durable on-disk engine
useCases: Distributed session state for ASP.NET and Java web farms
Low-latency shared object cache for .NET services
Real-time analytics and digital twins over fast-changing data
Replacing self-managed Redis in Windows-centric shops
